messages.content:
The world reforms. The crowd is massive, the largest Briar's ever seen. People from all walks of life, united for one singular purpose. To hear the music of Azalea Thompson. They talk amongst themselves, passing the time, locked in anticipation for the moment the concert will begin.

"I do hope she lives up to her reputation." Theo, sticking close to Briar's side to not lose her in the crowd, gives into the temptation of idle conversation.
Briar smiles "I'm sure she will Theo! Be excited"
He returns a bright smile. "Yes, perhaps we'll even be able to learn something."
She nods happily at him.

A booming voice carries over the crowd. "Ladies and gentlemen! Boys and girls! The moment you've all been waiting for! Prepare yourselves to be transfixed by the magical melodies of Azaleaaaaaaa Thompsoooooooon."

A woman dressed in a white suit steps onto stage. Her appearance is... worrying. Even from a good distance away, she clearly looks sickly, exhausted, and miserable.
Briar frowns at the sight. She looks over at Theo's face reading his expression
His brow has furrowed in concern, but his eyes remain locked on the stage, curious of how this will play out.
Gripping her skirt nervously, she looks back at the stage

Azalea examines the instruments lined up on stage. There's a wide variety, all painted pure white, adorned with her signature flower motif. She picks up the violin, and positions it to be played.

"How fortuitous. They say her instruments and set list are decided purely on whims during her concerts." Theo exposits.
She pushes her worry aside, focusing on the show. "That's so interesting! I'm so lucky she picked the violin this time."

Azalea concentrates, and her hands begin to move wildly. There is no discipline to her playing, but just as little doubt. It's as if the movements simply come naturally, without a single thought to their placement. Her face is intense, she's clearly pouring every piece of her soul into the song, translating herself into melody.

It's beautiful. A sense of wonder washes over the crowd, transfixed by the radiant and inspirational notes crafted not but a moment ago. All of life's worries seem to melt away, leaving only the present moment.
Briar closes her eyes, and a bright, wide smile appears on her face. She takes in every note, occasionally opening her eyes to watch how Azalea's hands move, admiring her talent.
It's difficult to glean much actual information on Azalea's techniques, both due to the distance and the almost inhuman speed her hands move at. Even then, she's clearly a master of her craft.
She turns to Theo, pulling him close to whisper in his ear "I told you she would live up to her reputation."
"I suppose you did. It is quite magnificent." He gives Briar a smirk, and rustles her hair. "Of course, I already get to hear a little prodigy of my own at home, don't I?"
She giggles "I'm not that good!"
"Hm, perhaps I'll be needing to replace you, then...?" He acts as if considering the idea. "Well, you are still younger than her. We'll give it a few years."
She pouts and looks away, crossing her arms, pretending to look upset

Theo chuckles, and returns his attention to the stage. The concert will continue without issue, each song as beautiful and inspiring as the last. She'll cycle through numerous instruments, a master of each she picks up. Not a single note will be played out of tune, for Briar, dreaming away in Paradise, certainly has no memory of such an event.

The music shifts suddenly. Something about it is off, but impossible to place. It's as if the very feeling it creates vacates Briar's body. All that remains is a wild sequence of random notes piercing her ears.
Briar covers her ears, trying to block out the piercing noise
The crowd fades, crumbling to sand one at a time. All that remains are Briar, Theo, and Azalea still pounding away at her poor instrument. It doesn't really matter which one.
She turns towards Theo, still covering one of her ears with one of her hands, and pulls at his sleeve trying to get his attention

The cohesion of his form is broken by her tug. His arm crumbles into sand, blown away by the wind. It travels from there, ultimately reaching a face still transfixed by a melody that Briar's ears are no longer fit for. In the blink of an eye, he's gone.
Panic fully kicks in. Scared, without knowing what else to do, she starts running towards Azalea
She lets go of her instrument, letting it tumble to the ground limply. Her miserable eyes stare down Briar, waiting for her to reach the stage.
Briar runs towards the side of the stage and quickly makes her way up the stairs towards Azelea. Briar stretches her hand towards her, but she hesitates, scared she will crumble into sand too
Azalea nods towards Briar. Her eyes have deep, dark circles under them, and she seems liable to collapse from exhaustion at any moment. "Hey."
Briar stares at her eyes, pondering what to do. "Will you also disappear if I touch you...?"
"I doubt it. They were just echoes, or... memories, I guess. I don't think I'm a memory. You don't remember talking to me, right?" She takes out a maraca, beginning to idly shake it to a rhythm.
Briar looks at the maraca confused "I... I don't remember"
"Yeah." She sets off towards the backstage area. "I don't really want to have this conversation twice. Let's go to a neutral meeting place."
"Oh-" she quickly follows after her

As Briar enters the backstage, the world shifts, almost imperceptibly. It becomes... vaguer. It becomes difficult to say for certain that Briar is still at that concert in Bander, but it would be just as difficult to prove otherwise. Azalea stands ahead of her, but just past her stands a woman Briar should not know, one she has not yet met.

Despite the impossibility, Briar recognizes her instinctively. A name flashes through her mind. She's face to face with "Bucky".

The world reforms. Calamari stands beside her mother, who waits with some form of anticipation, though certainly not excitement. They are two amongst many, standing in a massive crowd faced towards a stage. Azalea Thompson has come to Calamari's hometown of Farmton for a performance.

I peer up at the stage, wondering why Pearl even bothered bringing me with. Am I just here to tell her that she's better than Azalea? It shouldn't be too difficult to lie, if that's what she wants, but I'm not sure that she'd care either way. I've never had the ear for this kind of thing. And if I did, it would have been sanded down over the years anyways by the endless screeching practice sessions in the room next to mine. She's certainly never asked my opinion on those.

"Hm. Do you think she'll live up to her REPUTATION, Calamari? I somehow doubt it. I'll bet she only has fans because this is the ONLY performance these people will go to all year." She begins speaking.

I look around uncomfortably, hoping that the noise of the crowd is drowning her out. "Oh, well, I mean... you'll always be number one to me, mom...?" I test the bounds of what she wants from this conversation.

She looks down towards Calamari, considering her next words. "What a prize. One fan against this whole crowd. You've given me all I could ask for, Calamari." She rubs her forehead. "I should've brought something to DRINK."
I wish she had.
Is the performance set to start soon?

"Ladies and gentlemen, we apologize for the delay!" A voice carries over the crowd. "The sensation sweeping the nation, the flower of our empire, the one and only Azalea Thompson!" 

As the cheering of the crowd reaches its peak, a small, sickly-looking woman dressed in pure white skulks onto stage. Every instrument arranged in front of her shares the same coloration, along with bearing a distinctive mark of a flower. She looks them over, wearing a miserable expression, and ultimately picks up a saxophone in what almost appears to be a random selection.
She looks... not hyped to be here. Huh. I guess we've got something in common.

I haven't heard much saxophone music in my time, but the color-coding here seems to be trying to tell me that it's the exact same as everything else. I don't think whatever designer she hired is a fan of hers.
But, whatever. Maybe it'll get my mind off of... stuff.

She places the mouthpiece of the instrument against her lips, and a melody begins to flow out, guided by her nimble fingers. It's beautiful. An incredible, unbelievable tune. Calamari finds herself unable to look away, unable to not recognize and understand the joy of life that the song is communicating. It's as if it's holding onto her and refusing to let go.

Oh... my god. I blink, opening and closing my eyes a few times as I try to take it in. It's like... the music is melting into my skin... a salve, or a lotion? And... it understands. It's aligned with the air it's running through, with the... the aura of the earth, or... I don't know how to put it into words, fuck. Everything I come up with sounds idiotic. But I don't need to come up with the right words in my head. I can just feel it. This is what music should be, this is the essence of it. I bob back and forth, calm and heavy.

Yes. That's right. Calamari moves to the beat. To the tune washing over her. Washing over the entire crowd. Everyone here feels it. Even Pearl, though she would never admit it. This is the reason the world exists. For the sake of this very moment. The concert will continue. She will play song after song, using instrument after instrument, communicating a love deeper than any words can possibly convey. Thusly, Azalea Thompson will not utter a single word on this stage.

The first song finishes, she places the saxophone to the side. And looks straight into her eyes. Calamari's eyes. "Hey."
I wave at her dreamily, a wobbly smile on my face.
She does not return the wave. She looks at Calamari with the eyes of one who just got covered in the contents of a stranger's stomach at a bar. "Don't do that. Just get up here."
I point at myself questioningly.
Me?

"Who else?" She motions to Calamari's surroundings. It seems as if they're the only two present in this concert hall. The rest aren't relevant to this, and events already aren't as Calamari should remember. Maybe they all left, or died, or were hallucinations all along.
Weird... but it's a good thing Pearl isn't here to see this... ehehe. She would be so pissed off...
I drift towards Azalea's stage, her and me alone in the void of the world.
"Encore?"

"What is... wrong with you?" She spits this question out, flavoring it with a venomous tone. Nonetheless, she picks up the nearest instrument, a hurdy-gurdy. "I'll play it backstage. It'll be easier to talk there."
I follow the mean lady backstage.
A special performance... just for me... how could I ever forget this wonderful night? Where all is right in the world.

As Calamari steps backstage, the world... might shift. It's unclear if she's merely moved several feet, or several miles. All that matters for this meeting to occur is that either possibility remains open. Azalea has come to a stop ahead of Calamari, and past her is a woman Calamari will not meet for several years. Yet, here she is.

Briar McGregor. As Calamari comes face to face with this woman, that name comes naturally to her, as if nothing could be more obvious.

At at least one point in time, and in at least one city, Azalea stands backstage at at least one of her concerts. To one side of her stands Briar McGregor, while "Bucky" stands to the other.

"That's better. There's hardly enough of me to spread thin." Azalea's voice contains a sliver of relief.
"Hm... you... you're Briar, right? Have we met?" I cock my head inquisitively.
Briar crosses her arm looking nervous "Bucky... I don't know... You are familiar"
"Well, I have one of those faces."
"Okay." Azalea opens a door to another backstage room. Within it, three chairs surround a small table, fully stocked with a tea set. "We're gonna be here a while, let's get comfortable."
"Ahaha... I wonder what I did to earn a backstage meal with my favorite musician... luckyyy..."
"Yes ma'am..." quickly she walks towards one of the chairs
Azalea's eye twitches, but she ignores it and takes another seat. As she sits, she places a hurdy-gurdy in her lap, and quickly begins turning its crank to produce a tune.
Briar stares at the instrument, listening to the tune
I take my seat and lean towards Azalea, putting my chin in my hands. This is what it's all about, riiight...? This feeling... of understanding, of letting go... things will be okay. I can feel it.
"Stop being a fucking creep." Azalea directs this towards Bucky.
"Y-yes, ma'am... hehe. Sorry." The smile doesn't leave my face.
Her eyes move away from the instrument towards Bucky's face. Analyzing every feature.

Strange as it is, Briar definitely remembers Bucky's face.

Continuing to play her hurdy-gurdy, Azalea sighs. "Look, I didn't even want to talk to you guys, so just don't make this more painful than it has to be. I'm just doing this as a favor to Sunatra."
"Who is Sunatra?"
"Empy..."
"You know... the emperor."
"I guess most people aren't on a first name basis with him, yeah. Whatever, just habit. We can call him The Emperor if that works."
"Well, it works for me..."
I glance over at the mysterious Briar. "You good with it?"
Briar nods slowly "I suppose..."

"A name can't carry a person's character anyway. It's all just an excuse to make up our own perceptions. It's no more a real form of communication than words, or music." She says with her words as she continues to play music.
"Hm... can I ask, why are we here?"
"To listen to the music, Briar... she's a musician. You should know that, since you're at her concert..."
"Now, can you quiet down? You have a cute voice, admittedly, but... she asked us not to talk..."
"Sorry, Ms. Thompson..."
"I'm sorry..." she whispers

"I literally did not do that." She pours herself a cup of coffee from the tea pot. "You're here to learn about me, as hypocritical as that is. I'm not a narcissist; this is, again, just a favor. I'm sure talking about myself is gonna be like pulling teeth, so you better listen the first time."

"You said, um... you definitely said that you didn't want to talk to us... so we shouldn't... I think? I'm pretty sure. I probably just misunderstood. But you really don't have to pull your teeth... it's fine! It's fine if you don't talk about yourself. I'm fine with it, Briar is fine with it..."
I glare at Briar.
"Right?"
"Sure..."

"Is there something wrong with you? Like, mentally?" She chugs the cup of coffee. "Look, even being here right now feels like being stabbed all over. Tiny little knives carving away at me. I'm not happy about it, but I'm never happy. If you're at my concert, it's obvious you don't have an original bone in your body. Just taking in my music and spewing out what you think you hear. I get that, but at least try to act normal, okay?"
I frown, the enjoyable haze breaking somewhat. "Wait, do you want me to act original or normal?"
"Those are opposites."
"Are you okay Azalea? Is there anything I can do to help you...?"

"No, it's... I'm fine now." She straightens out a little. "I just can't stand those drooling sycophants who treat my songs like gospel. They think just because they happen to overhear me playing some music for myself, they know me personally or something. It's almost as disturbing as it is just sad."
"I understand that feeling, not to the extent you do, but something similar"
"I didn't hear you playing music for yourself, though. I'm sorry if people have annoyed you, but my- you charged good money to allow people in here. You invited us to listen?"

"I don't set these things up. It's all the Emperor's cronies, and their cronies, and so on. I play music no matter where I am. I have to. Every now and then, they'll set up a stage and tell me to stand there for a bit. It's more like a zoo than a concert, honestly." She seems less bitter about this than previous topics, at least.
"That's... rough. I'm sorry. I don't think you should be forced to do things that seem unnatural to you. I'm grateful for this private event, though. Hopefully this isn't... the same."
"That's horrible" Briar gets teary eyes
"Is it the same? Is somebody forcing you to be here?"
"I'm not *forced*, it's... Ugh, you're not getting it. Maybe I should just start from the beginning."
"If you are comfortable, please"
"If you want to, yeah."

"The Emperor found me as a baby. Basically, I'm an orphan. Not that unusual of a sob story, obviously, but the circumstances are a bit unique. Most orphans don't murder their parents the day they're born."
I consider what she means. Did her mother die in childbirth, and maybe... the father killed himself? And she blames herself for the collapse of the loving family. That's... morbid.
Briar opens her eyes widely "What... what do you mean?"

Azalea considers her own words. "You know, now that I think about it, I guess most orphans don't murder their parents at all. I mean, I don't have statistics on that, but still, it seems right. I guess my sense of normal is just skewed a bit. Anyway, Bucky should know what I mean. Remember that sandstorm you two were caught up in? It's like that."
"Hm."
"No, I don't think there was a sandstorm."
"It was pretty nice outside just now."
Briar tilts her head thinking trying to recall

She pinches the bridge of her nose. "Fine. We'll do it the hard way." Pouring another cup of coffee, she continues. "My body has... well, it's a bit hard to define. It's been described as a defense mechanism, or an allergic reaction, or... I just think of it as a rejection, I guess. A rejection of this world. This painful, sick world. Whenever I wake up from a deep sleep..." She balls her hand into a fist, and then opens it. "Boom. Anything too close is just gone, turned to ash. Then comes the heat, then the shockwaves. Basically, you don't wanna be within like a mile of me, to put it mildly."

I open my mouth in shock. "But... your music is so beautiful, Azalea! How could you think that the world is *sick?* When I heard it... all I could think about was how much wonder there was in it, how *correct* it all was. How can you *make* something like that when you think it's all diseased? That's... so sad. I'm so sorry."
"How- How is that possible?"

"I get the feeling you two are asking very different questions." She rolls her eyes. "I'll start with the easier one. I can make that music because that's what it's *about*. Every song I play is a crystalization of this choking agony I feel. I'm up there screaming into my instruments, pouring out my hatred and vitriol through them and into melodic form, and you bastards just make up your own meaning instead of actually *listening*. It's not even your meaning, not really, but it's certainly not mine. It's just some... twisted, misunderstanding. Some funhouse mirror version of me that slowly replaces you as you listen."
"Music is an outlet for every emotion and feeling... it breaks my heart yours are only negative ones"

An annoyed expression washes over my face. "I'm not being replaced by anyone, Azalea. Sorry if we have different artistic interpretations or whatever, but if I was turning into you, I'd notice the differences pretty quickly, I promise. You make good music."

"No, I don't, but that's good. It's important." She takes a sip. "The Emperor had me put under careful watch, and his top researchers figured out a way to... mitigate the damage. If I don't sleep, I can't explode. My body has another odd quirk. Music physically hurts me to hear. That's the pain I was describing earlier. The pain is good. It keeps me awake. It keeps others safe. Playing it hurts, but it keeps the pain inside me. Keeps it from leaking."
"I was always under the impression that sleep deprivation that extreme would kill you anyways."

Her sunken, hollow eyes stare miserably at Bucky. "It's not exactly healthy, no. Still, I sleep enough to live. Barely. Have to go out in the middle of nowhere, but I manage. Personally, I think that's where I should stay. Maybe then I could get some real shut-eye. Live out some wonderful days in a world with no need for words or music... but the Emperor wants me to tour. Here, let's have some audience participation. Any guesses as to why he drags a weapon of mass destruction around the nation?"
"Not really. Have you considered blowing him up?"
I give Briar a side-eye to check if she's going to report me for treason or something.
Briar looks teary eyed, lost in thought "I- It could be greed, it could be so you aren't lonely..."
"Your music is still beautiful... and even if you are dangerous because of your condition, it isn't your fault... you shouldn't be forced to live alone"
"Haven't you been listening? I'm always alone, even around other people." She waves her hand dismissively. "Whatever, whatever. Look, just... what do you guys think music *is*?"
"I'm sorry" she sighs

"Before tonight, I would have just said it was a job. But after hearing you... wow. I don't know anymore. I guess I'd have to agree with you that it's a form of communication, even though you seem to be communicating yourself... pretty poorly. Maybe the conversation I'm having just isn't with you."
"Music... is magic." She looks dead serious. "Every song, every note... playing it is casting a spell."
"It is magical" she whispers "Music is my reason to live, it's a language that can communicate so much"
"Yeah... you're right, Briar. They're the same thing... magic is the language of the universe."
"When I play a song, all my fears, all the pain in my heart, it all disappears. Very different from your experience" she looks at Azalea "But my pain isn't even a fraction close to yours"

Her brows furrow in frustration. "I'm not speaking in fucking... riddles here, okay? I'm being literal. I'm a wizard. Every musician is, whether they realize it or not. Some are just better than others. Me? I'm the best around. That's why the Emperor parades me around. To brainwash his subjects."
((End session))
"A wizard?" Briar tilts her head "Brainwash...?"

I tilt my head too, before realizing that it looks like I'm copying the other girl and righting it again. "Magic-magic isn't exactly... I mean, honestly, I'm not sure it was ever a thing, but it's not, like- if every musician was a magician, I'd classify that as it being pretty *commonplace.* I think I would have heard. I'm not inclined to conspiratorial thinking, Azalea."

"Most are just weak magicians. Or bad musicians, I guess. Their magic is in the air, but not really... doing anything. Leaving it as it is. How do I explain..." She motions to the side of the backstage Bucky entered from. "Look, you felt it, right? The way my music rearranged your mind. Were those really things you thought? Or just a spell telling you what to think? What to *be*?"
"Those were my thoughts." I say it without hesitation. "I believed those things. I still do. If magic is telling me who to be, I can promise it's not yours."
She groans. "Okay, you're impossible to talk to." Azalea turns to Briar before continuing. "You're like me. Cursed from birth. Do you understand... or at least, believe?"
"Me?" She points at herself
"Hm- I believe in magic I suppose... I believe in those magical creatures and stuff from the books I would read... But I'm a little confused about what you mean"
I roll my eyes.

"Magic, at its core, is just... changing one thing into another. A ball of fire born from the air. An soldier born from clay. Immortality born from the mortal world. You can boil it down to the ability to change things. So, we must ask what makes something itself."
"That's so complicated"
"Magic always looked like things just happen because a fairy wanted it to be that way"
"No, no, wait, I have the ability to change things already. Everyone does. That can't be the definition, that's stupid."
"Hm, funny, I didn't think you'd be the one into fairies." She takes a sip of coffee. "You can change things *about* something. But you can't truly turn it into something else. Not without magic."
"How do you truly turn it into something else? How do you make your magic work? Is it colorful and exciting?"
"Have you heard of... cooking?"

"It... could be exciting, I guess. The Emperor likes for me to work subtly. Even if he didn't though... I may be the best wizard alive, but that last part does a lot of heavy lifting. Magic's faded a lot. It's basically all dried up by now." She turns to Bucky, reluctantly. "What? What are you even talking about?"
"You can turn something into something else. You can mix flour and water and, um... other stuff into bread. It's not flour anymore."
"You wouldn't eat flour."
"There's been an essential change."
She seems relieved. "Yeah. Exactly. Magic."
Briar tilts her head
"but everyone can cook to a certain extent... Does how good you are at cooking mean how magical you are?"

"Look, if cooking is *magic,* then *most people* are magicians. I can probably find other things you'd tell me are magic too. Why even have the term? Why even have the classification? The world is magic! Fine, I can get behind that, whatever, but it's not a real, like, conversation... that you can have."
"If I'm bad at cooking... Does that mean I don't have magic? So is my music not magical? Or is it like... Different categories?"
"No, no, don't listen to her... you're magical either way, alright?" I smile at her. This seems like the best way to approach the topic right now.

"You're not a jockey just because you got on a horse. Normal people can make use of crude forms of magic, but they're not wizards. It takes true talent to do what I do. Magic is just one small part of cooking, but it's the entire life of a musician."
She nods with a smile at Bucky and looks back at Azalea, her face completely serious "Can I do magic then?"

"Obviously." She taps her tea cup, trying to find the right words. "Alright, let's talk about cooking bread, sure. Each recipe is made up of different ingredients, right? Dough's made up of... whatever it was you said. Flower? And then you apply heat, changing what the object is made up of. Agreed?"
"Yeah, that sounds right. Some other things, too, but basically."
"Wait, is fire magic?"

"It's not the fire that's magic. It's what it's doing. Each piece of the dough, each tiny piece of the flower, has its own ingredients. Little, invisible particles. Linked in a certain way. Vibrating against each other at a certain frequency. Heat is just lots of really fast vibrations. Like when you rub your hands together in the cold. Those vibrations break apart the links, and form new ones. The reason it's no longer a flower is because the things that make up a flower have to be arranged in a flower-like way. And now they're arranged in a bread-like way."
I crook my eyebrow. "No, not *a* flower. Flour. The white dust. Why would I believe you about this when you don't even know what we're talking about? When you think bread is invisible?"
Briar looks back and forth at Azalea and Bucky but slowly zones out, looking up and around the room

"Anything is invisible if you're big enough." She picks up a container on the table and pours some white dust into her beverage. "I can see crowds at my concerts, but each person is just an invisible part of the whole."
"I'm confused..." she looks back at them
"Me too, buddy. I feel like I shouldn't even have to respond to that last bit, it's so transparently meaningless."

She sighs as she mixes her drink. "Look the... the specifics aren't important. Let's say it like this. Magic exists in the future relative to what it touches. When you use magic, you're changing something from the past to the future. You can do this blindly, like with a fire. Irreversibly removing the past in a blaze of passing time. Or, you can do it precisely. You can arrange your music in a certain way, create vibrations holding information, blueprints of the future, and send them out. Rearranging something in a specific, preset pattern, diffusing the future and past into a present of your design."
"You get it now?"
"Hm."
"I think so"
"Well, presuming I do get it, and ignoring my disgust at the whole concept for a second. Words would be the strongest form of magic, wouldn't they? But you're not a singer. Why is that?"

"..." She grimaces. "It's disgusting watching those pigs eat their slop. I pour my heart into my songs, but they can't hear me. Not really. It'd just be all that more painful if tore my words to shreds too."
"Oh? And we're just pigs to you, too, I guess?"
"What if you did it for yourself? If you like singing you should"
"Come on. Don't be so cruel to pigs." She waves her hand dismissively at Bucky. "I *don't* like singing. It... it burns. I can't be a part of that future. That recipe everyone is marching towards."
I sneer at her, taking the insult. There's a part of me that was hoping I could goad her into singing for us, but... it wouldn't have worked, anyways. Probably. Ugh.

"Fine, then. No vocal music, I guess. But we're talking, aren't we? You're trying to use words to change how our minds are laid out, to rearrange the future with your informational vibrations. How well are you managing against us sub-swine?"

"Not great, considering you don't believe anything I've said. I've never been great at talking, but no one is, really. They just pretend like they can understand each other. Like the little puppets of other people in their minds are the real things. With that delusion, they move forward. I couldn't do that." She takes her cup, and pours its steaming contents onto her hand.
"OH! Are you okay?" she gaps, stands up and walks towards her

I flinch, then stand up with Briar. "Why would you do that? Okay, alright. Um, there are probably medical supplies at a concert venue, right? Wait here." I tear off a strip of my shirt to repurpose into a makeshift bandage. Magic.

Her hand is completely unharmed, just wet. The skin has no signs of burns. "I saw the way you looked at me. In the crater. I've been seeing it my whole life. When people understand what I am. What I can do to them. When they look their death in the eye." She stumbles to her feet, as if possessed, knocking over her chair. "And they lie, lie, lie. They smile. They keep me as long as they have to. Until they can throw me to the next. And the next. And the next. But me? I'm just me. Just me. A whole world inside me no one will see. Worlds inside them they won't let me be."
"Oh, I... I thought that was a lot hotter than it was. Damn." I look down at my ruined shirt with a sad expression.
"Anyways, I don't really know what you're talking about. Sorry. If you want my help with something, you'll have to ask."
"Hm- I don't fully understand what you say most of the time but- I enjoy speaking with you, I enjoy your presence, if that means anything to you"

"If anyone could... it'd be *you*." She stares at Briar with disgust. "A child no one wanted. A burden to everyone she's ever met. A mistake that won't just do everyone a favor and..." She grips her head tightly, almost as if trying to break it in two.
"Oh... I- My brother cares about me... he is... he is the only one but I have someone" her voice gets quieter and quieter as she speaks

"Just me. Just me. I won't let them *change* me. I won't listen to their music. To my music. I won't let it bring me to their future. A parody of the truth. I'll remain. A stone in the desert.
